exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Strong room-design work proves every area and cost — here is how one student planned a backyard patio.

traits.trait: Shows the area formula with units
traits.sample: My patio is 9 ft by 7 ft, so the area is 9 × 7 = 63 square feet — I labeled it ft² so no one confuses it with length.
traits.why: The formula, the substitution, and the correct units all appear.

traits.trait: Multiplies area by unit cost step by step
traits.sample: Pavers cost $3.25 per square foot, so 63 ft² × $3.25 = $204.75 for the whole patio.
traits.why: Cost per square foot times area is written out, not just a final price.

traits.trait: Breaks a tricky shape into rectangles
traits.sample: My patio has a corner cut out, so I split it into two rectangles, found each area, and added them.
traits.why: Decomposing composite shapes is the key Unit 5 move.

traits.trait: Judges whether the price fits the range
traits.sample: $3.25 per ft² lands in the middle of the typical $2–$6 range, so my choice is realistic, not luxury.
traits.why: Comparing to real-world ranges shows number sense, not just arithmetic.
